([[Johns Creek, Georgia]]) | college = [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] (2013–2017) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] (2016) * Third-team All-ACC (2017) * ACC Most Improved Player (2016) }} '''Jaron Blossomgame''' (born September 16, 1993) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for [[Clemson University]]. == High school career == Blossomgame attended [[Chattahoochee High School]] in [[Johns Creek, Georgia]]. He played high school basketball with the Cougars under head coach Kacey Martin. After his junior season, he earned first-team all-region and second-team all-state after averaging 24 points and 8.8 rebounds per game. As a senior, Blossomgame helped Chattahoochee end the season with a 25–5 record, as his team qualified for the Sweet 16 round of the state tournament.{{cite web|title=Jaron Blossomgame|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205562325|website=''ClemsonTigers.com''|accessdate=21 March 2016}} He joined the Georgia Stars of the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) in 2011 and led his team with 15.7 points per game. However, that year, Blossomgame broke his leg while trying to dunk with his trainer. His bone protruded from his left leg at the time.{{cite web|last1=Walton|first1=Carroll Rogers|title=Blossomgame leading way for Clemson|url=http://www.myajc.com/news/sports/college-basketball/leg-injury-behind-him-alpharettas-blossomgame-lead/nppYn/|date=December 12, 2015|website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|accessdate=21 March 2016}} After the injury, he expected to wear a [[orthopedic cast|cast]] for the following six to eight weeks.{{cite web|title=Update on Blossomgame's broken leg|url=http://www.tigernet.com/update/recruit/Update-Blossomgames-broken-leg-5547?prevbox=1|website=TigerNet|accessdate=21 March 2016}} ==College career== Blossomgame chose [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] over [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]], [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech]] and [[Gardner-Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball|Gardner-Webb]]. He elected to [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 season]] due to the broken leg suffered in AAU.{{cite web|last1=Johnson|first1=Raphielle|title=Clemson freshman forward Jaron Blossomgame announces decision to redshirt|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2012/11/15/clemson-freshman-forward-jaron-blossomgame-announces-decision-to-redshirt/|date=November 15, 2012|website=[[NBCSports.com]]|accessdate=April 30, 2017}} After two seasons of steadily-improving production, Blossomgame enjoyed a breakout junior season in [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]]. Blossomgame averaged 18.7 points and 6.7 rebounds per game and became the 13th Clemson player to be named first-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). He was also named the conference's Most Improved Player for the season.{{cite web|last1=|first1=|title=Clemson’s Jaron Blossomgame named first team All-ACC|url=http://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article64618327.html|date=March 7, 2016|website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|accessdate=April 30, 2017}} Following the season, Blossomgame declared his eligibility for the [[2016 NBA draft]], and was invited to the [[NBA Draft Combine]].{{cite web|last1=Hope|first1=Dan|title=Jaron Blossomgame’s stock rising after NBA Draft Combine|url=http://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article78789722.html|date=May 20, 2016|website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|accessdate=April 30, 2017}} Ultimately, he chose to return to Clemson for his senior season.{{cite web|last1=|first1=|title=Clemson's Jaron Blossomgame withdraws from NBA draft|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15727303/clemson-forward-jaron-blossomgame-pulls-nba-draft|date=May 25, 2016|website=[[ESPN.com]]|accessdate=April 30, 2017}} Blossomgame was named to the preseason All-ACC team and was named a preseason [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by several publications.{{cite web|last1=|first1=|title=Blossomgame Preseason All-ACC|url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=211251701|date=October 25, 2016|website=clemsontigers.com|accessdate=April 30, 2017}} Blossomgame averaged 17.7 points and 6.3 rebounds and led the Tigers to the [[2017 National Invitation Tournament]], earning third-team All-ACC honors.{{cite web|last1=Raynor|first1=Grace|title=Clemson forward Jaron Blossomgame named to third-team All-ACC|url=http://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson-forward-jaron-blossomgame-named-to-third-team-all-acc/article_263735f4-01e8-11e7-9f61-9f97c813118f.html|date=March 5, 2017|website=[[The Post and Courier]] |accessdate=April 30, 2017}} He was also a finalist for the [[Senior CLASS Award]], earning second-team senior All-American honors.{{cite web|last1=|first1=|title=Villanova’s Josh Hart Wins 2016-17 Senior CLASS Award for Men’s Basketball|url=http://www.seniorclassaward.com/news/view/villanovas_josh_hart_wins_2016-17_senior_class_award_for_mens_basketball/|date=March 31, 2017|website=seniorclassaward.com |accessdate=April 30, 2017}} After his last year at Clemson ended, Blossomgame was invited to his second straight [[NBA Draft Combine]] event, becoming one of the first players to ever get invited to the event multiple times in different years. == References == {{Reflist|2}} ==External links==
